The course is built on a human-first, tool-based teaching philosophy, with no slides, no decks, and no theoretical lectures.

**Decisions Made & Alternatives Ruled Out:**
- **Format:** A live 6-week cohort was chosen over self-paced modules or a 6-week drip release. The cohort model was selected for higher completion rates, stronger community, and better retention — especially for non-technical learners who thrive on structure and human presence.
- **Platform:** Coursemint was eliminated due to video buffering in India and Brazil. A new platform was not named, but the core requirements are: global CDN for video, live screen sharing with device control, low-latency playback, and full control over student data and access. It uses tight jump-cuts on talking-head segments, with real-time SQL queries overlaid as floating captions during screen shares. This style was validated by beta testers and is now the only approved format.

**Context Note: Practical SQL for Analysts – Course Development Summary**

The course, *Practical SQL for Analysts*, is a live 6-week cohort designed for business and data analysts who need to write SQL to answer real business questions — not for database engineers or developers. The course is built on a human-first, tool-based teaching philosophy: no slides, no decks, no theory. All instruction occurs through live screen-share demos in actual SQL tools (e.g., DB Fiddle, BigQuery, SQL Server), with real-time typing, errors, and fixes.

The teaching style, refined with editor Ruben, uses tight jump-cut editing on talking-head segments, with floating query captions overlaid during screen shares. This format was tested with beta users and proven effective for clarity, retention, and engagement. It is now the official house style.

The course structure is 6 weeks, with one 45-minute live session per week. Each session follows a consistent rhythm: a business question is posed, the solution is built in real time, and common errors are debugged on screen. The Capstone project, named *The Compass Project*, is a real-world analysis of a messy, public dataset (e.g., retail sales, customer churn). It is unlocked at the start of Week 4, after foundational skills are solidified. Students submit 5–7 queries and a 1–2 page narrative summary.

The course is not sold with lifetime access. All pricing is one-time, with three tiers:  
- **Core ($199)**: 8 modules, video + PDFs, 30-day access  
- **Plus ($299)**: Core + Capstone + 1:1 feedback  
- **Pro ($499)**: All above + 30-day community access + 3 Q&A sessions with the instructor  

Platform choice was made after eliminating Coursemint due to global buffering issues (especially in India and Brazil). The solution is a custom LMS built on Thinkific + Vimeo + Zoom integration, prioritizing low-latency video, global CDN performance, and full control over delivery.

Student emails and payment relationships are owned by the instructor — not the platform. This ensures long-term access, follow-up capability, and community control.

The student community is structured as a private Discord (optional) and a public forum within the course portal. It is self-sustaining: weekly "Query of the Week" prompts trigger student-to-student help. The instructor only responds to 1–2 high-quality submissions per week (≤10 minutes). Peer review is encouraged via upvotes and replies.

The sandbox is a shared, real-time database environment (e.g., DB Fiddle) where students run practice queries. It is not a platform billing sandbox. It is not expected to handle 200 students simultaneously — the course is designed for 50–200 students, with live sessions capped at 100. No student will "hammer" it — usage is distributed and guided.

The course does not use YouTube for lead generation. The prior 3-part mini-course failed (40 hours → 9 signups). Instead, a new lead magnet will be built: a 30-minute "SQL for Real Questions" video, sent via a simple landing page.

The CE credit contact at the analysts’ association is Wilhelmina Choo — to be contacted if CE credits are ever offered.

Open threads:

- Setting up the first "Query of the Week" prompt  
- Launching the first beta cohort (target: 20 students)

All decisions were made to protect teaching integrity, learner experience, and instructor sustainability. No fluff, no lifetime access, no platform dependency.
